SMAC3 builds on top of existing GP implementations and offers several acquisition functions, including LCB ( [Srinivas et al., 2010](https://arxiv.org/html/2109.09831#bib.bib39 "")), TS ( [Thompson, 1933](https://arxiv.org/html/2109.09831#bib.bib40 "")),
PI and EI ( [Jones et al., 1998](https://arxiv.org/html/2109.09831#bib.bib22 "")) and variants, e.g., EI per second ( [Snoek et al., 2012](https://arxiv.org/html/2109.09831#bib.bib38 "")) for evaluations with different runtimes and logEI ( [Hutter et al., 2010](https://arxiv.org/html/2109.09831#bib.bib19 "")) for heavy-tailed cost distributions. The pre-set of SMAC4BB follows commonly used components and comprises a Sobol sequence as initial design, a GP with 5/2-Matérn Kernel and EI as acquisition function, similar to [Snoek et al. (2012)](https://arxiv.org/html/2109.09831#bib.bib38 "").
### 2.2 SMAC4HPO: SMAC for CASH and Structured Hyperparameter Optimization

SMAC3 can also tackle the combined algorithm selection and hyperparameter optimization problem (CASH) ( [Thornton et al., 2013](https://arxiv.org/html/2109.09831#bib.bib41 "")), and searches for a well-performing AiA\_{i} from a _set of algorithms_ 𝐀\\mathbf{A} and its hyperparameters 𝝀∈𝚲i\\boldsymbol{\\lambda}\\in\\boldsymbol{\\Lambda}\_{i}:

|     |     |     |     |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | (A∗,𝝀∗)∈arg​minAi∈𝐀,𝝀∈𝚲i⁡c​(Ai,𝝀)=arg​minAi∈𝐀,𝝀∈𝚲i⁡ℒ​(𝒟train,𝒟val,Ai​(𝝀)).(A^{\*},\\boldsymbol{\\lambda}^{\*})\\in\\argmin\_{A\_{i}\\in\\mathbf{A},\\boldsymbol{\\lambda}\\in\\boldsymbol{\\Lambda}\_{i}}c(A\_{i},\\boldsymbol{\\lambda})=\\argmin\_{A\_{i}\\in\\mathbf{A},\\boldsymbol{\\lambda}\\in\\boldsymbol{\\Lambda}\_{i}}\\mathcal{L}(\\mathcal{D}\_{\\text{train}},\\mathcal{D}\_{\\text{val}};A\_{i}(\\boldsymbol{\\lambda})). |  | (2) |

The hyperparameter sub-space 𝚲i\\boldsymbol{\\Lambda}\_{i} for an algorithm AiA\_{i} is only active if AiA\_{i} was chosen. Therefore, there is a conditional hierarchy structure between the top-level hyperparameter choosing AiA\_{i} and the subspace 𝚲i\\boldsymbol{\\Lambda}\_{i}.
SMAC3 models these spaces by using a random forest ( [Breimann, 2001](https://arxiv.org/html/2109.09831#bib.bib9 "")), with SMAC having been the first BO approach to use this type of model ( [Hutter et al., 2011](https://arxiv.org/html/2109.09831#bib.bib20 "")).
SMAC3 supports multiple levels of conditionalities, e.g., one top-level hyperparameter choosing a classification algorithm and another sub-level hyperparameter
an optimizer (for training NNs) enabling a second sub-level of hyperparameters.
The pre-set of SMAC4HPO is based on the tuning by [Lindauer et al. (2019b)](https://arxiv.org/html/2109.09831#bib.bib29 "") and combines a Sobol sequence as initial design, a RF as surrogate model and logEI as acquisition function.
### 2.3 SMAC4MF: SMAC for Expensive Tasks and Automated Deep Learning

On some HPO tasks, e.g., optimizing hyperparameters and architectures for deep learning, training many models might be too expensive.
Multi-fidelity optimization is a common approach, for cases where we can observe cheaper approximations of the true cost:

|     |     |     |     |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | 𝝀∗∈arg​min𝝀∈𝚲⁡c​(𝝀,bmax)=arg​min𝝀∈𝚲⁡ℒ​(𝒟train,𝒟val,𝝀,bmax).\\boldsymbol{\\lambda}^{\*}\\in\\argmin\_{\\boldsymbol{\\lambda}\\in\\boldsymbol{\\Lambda}}c(\\boldsymbol{\\lambda},b\_{max})=\\argmin\_{\\boldsymbol{\\lambda}\\in\\boldsymbol{\\Lambda}}\\mathcal{L}(\\mathcal{D}\_{\\text{train}},\\mathcal{D}\_{\\text{val}};\\boldsymbol{\\lambda},b\_{max}). |  | (3) |

Here, a configuration is evaluated with a budget b≤bm​a​xb\\leq b\_{max} (e.g., number of epochs, dataset size or channels of CNN) to obtain a cheap proxy of the true cost function at bm​a​xb\_{max}.
---
SMAC3 follows the principle of BOHB ( [Falkner et al., 2018](https://arxiv.org/html/2109.09831#bib.bib12 "")) in combining Hyperband ( [Li et al., 2018](https://arxiv.org/html/2109.09831#bib.bib26 "")) and BO, where the surrogate model is fitted on the highest budget-level with sufficient observations. However, its RF models tend to yield much better performance than BOHB’s TPE models, see Figure [2](https://arxiv.org/html/2109.09831#S3.F2 "Figure 2 ‣ 3 Brief Empirical Comparison ‣ SMAC3: A Versatile Bayesian Optimization Packagefor Hyperparameter Optimization") for illustrative examples.
With the exception of the RF, the pre-set of SMAC4MF is similar to [Falkner et al. (2018)](https://arxiv.org/html/2109.09831#bib.bib12 "") and consists of a random initial design and Hyperband as intensification method.
### 2.4 SMAC4AC: SMAC for Algorithm Configuration

A more general view on the problem of HPO is called algorithm configuration (AC) ( [Hutter et al., 2009](https://arxiv.org/html/2109.09831#bib.bib18 ""); [Ansótegui et al., 2009](https://arxiv.org/html/2109.09831#bib.bib1 ""); [López-Ibáñez\\
et al., 2016](https://arxiv.org/html/2109.09831#bib.bib30 "")), where the goal is to determine a well-performing robust configuration across a set of problem instances ii from a finite set ℐ\\mathcal{I}:

|     |     |     |     |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | 𝝀∗∈arg​min𝝀∈𝚲c(𝝀)=arg​min𝝀∈𝚲∑i∈ℐc′(𝝀,i)\\boldsymbol{\\lambda}^{\*}\\in\\argmin\_{\\boldsymbol{\\lambda}\\in\\boldsymbol{\\Lambda}}c(\\boldsymbol{\\lambda})=\\argmin\_{\\boldsymbol{\\lambda}\\in\\boldsymbol{\\Lambda}}\\sum\_{i\\in\\mathcal{I}}c^{\\prime}(\\boldsymbol{\\lambda},i) |  | (4) |

The origin of SMAC lies in AC ( [Hutter et al., 2011](https://arxiv.org/html/2109.09831#bib.bib20 "")).
It inherits the ideas of aggressive racing ( [Hutter et al., 2009](https://arxiv.org/html/2109.09831#bib.bib18 "")) which evaluates less promising candidate configurations on only a few instances, and to collect sufficient empirical evidence on many instances if the candidate could become the next incumbent configuration. Furthermore, SMAC3 supports imputation of right-censored observations and a logEI to model heavy-tailed cost distributions;
it also uses a customized hyperparameter configuration of the RF surrogate model for AC. SMAC successfully optimized configuration spaces with more than 300300 hyperparameters for SAT solvers ( [Hutter et al., 2017](https://arxiv.org/html/2109.09831#bib.bib21 "")), yielding speedups of up to several orders of magnitude.
The pre-set of SMAC4AC follows [Hutter et al. (2011)](https://arxiv.org/html/2109.09831#bib.bib20 "") and combines a single default configuration as initial design, a RF as surrogate model (with different hyperparameter settings compared to SMAC4HPO), logEI as acquisition function and aggressive racing as intensification mechanism.
